literal: External limbs all what use will they do to the body, if the internal limb, love, to those who lack?
translation: Of what use are all the outer limbs of the body to those who lack the inner limb of love?
modern: உள்ளத்து உறுப்பாகிய அன்பு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு, உடம்பின் வெளி உறுப்புகள் எல்லாம் என்ன பயனைச் செய்யும்?
explanation: This couplet compares love to an essential internal organ (அகத்துறுப்பு) of the body, while the physical limbs (like hands, eyes, and legs) are merely external organs (புறத்துறுப்பு). Just as a body cannot truly live or function without its vital internal organs, a human life is meaningless without the inner quality of love. For those who lack love in their hearts, having all external limbs intact is of no real value, as they cannot perform genuine acts of human connection. The poet uses the archaic verb form 'செய்பும்' to ask what useful action these outer limbs could possibly perform without the guiding force of love.
